title: UAE Logistics Brief
lede: Attacks in the Strait of Hormuz are at their worst level of the crisis: seven tankers hit since 16 November, three of them in 15 hours off Khasab. In the air, Dubai export rates to Europe are up 83% on last year, just as Amazon and noon run 12-day sales to 30 November.

gauges.note: Three in 15 hours on 20–21 Nov, 8–17 nm off Khasab (JMIC via Iran International, 22 Nov)

stories.headline: Seven tankers hit since 16 November; three in 15 hours off Khasab
body: The Joint Maritime Information Centre said on Sunday that seven tankers have been struck in the Strait of Hormuz since 16 November. The three latest were outbound ships hit on 20 and 21 November, 8 to 17 nautical miles from Khasab. Two were struck about 50 minutes apart.

Tracking data showed no transits by cargo ships above 1,000 deadweight tons between 19 and 21 November. On Saturday UKMTO reported two more tankers struck, with no casualties, and Bahrain intercepted several Iranian aerial attacks.
stories.soWhat: New since Friday: four more strikes and no cargo transits for three days. Treat Gulf sea capacity as shut for the rest of November.

stories.headline: Hormuz traffic down again: 263 transits in a week
body: UKMTO's weekly overview counted 263 transits in the seven days to 18 November, down from 308 the week before. Only 73 broadcast AIS. Six tankers were attacked in that week and two needed help.
UKMTO has logged 106 incidents in the strait since 28 February. JMIC rates the threat as severe.
stories.soWhat: The trend is still down, not stabilising. Do not promise customers a sea recovery date.

stories.headline: Oman's ports carry more Gulf cargo, including Saudi-bound loads
body: Gulf News reports that the UAE–Oman Green Corridors and the ports of Duqm and Sohar are being used to keep Gulf cargo moving, including cargo bound for Saudi Arabia.
Asyad has started a weekly Duqm–Khalifa Port Green Corridor by road through Khatm Al Shiklah and Al Ain Dry Port, and says it expects volumes to grow.
stories.soWhat: Oman-to-UAE road legs are now a standard route. We should sell them as a product, not a one-off fix.

stories.headline: Dubai air export rates up 83% to Europe as capacity stays tight
body: WorldACD says global air rates rose 2% in week 45 to $3.45 per kg, 31% above last year. Middle East and South Asia had the biggest annual rise of any region, at 63%.
Rates from Dubai to Europe are up 83% on last year, and Dubai to the US is up more than 80%. Air cargo weight into Saudi Arabia is down 33% against early October, after Houthi missile attacks.
stories.soWhat: Dubai outbound is the most expensive it has been in a year. Every air quote out of Dubai needs today's buy rate.

stories.headline: European airlines return to Dubai from 25 November
body: Lufthansa, SWISS and Eurowings plan to restart Dubai flights on 25 November, and Austrian Airlines on 12 December. Singapore Airlines stays off Dubai until 28 February 2027, and Finnair will not fly to Dubai this winter.
Etihad's Riyadh and Dammam passenger and cargo flights remain suspended to 30 November. EASA has extended its Iran and Iraq airspace advisories to 31 January 2027.
stories.soWhat: New since Friday: some Europe belly space comes back this week. It may ease Dubai–Europe rates a little in December.

stories.headline: UAE sales peak: Amazon and noon both run 12 days to 30 November
body: Amazon's White Friday sale started on 19 November and runs to 30 November across more than 30 categories. noon's Yellow Friday runs on the same dates, with up to 90% off and up to 80% off on noon Minutes.
Amazon cites HarrisX research that 85% of UAE shoppers are more likely to buy during sales events.
stories.soWhat: This is the biggest parcel week of the year for UAE last mile. Returns will follow in early December.

competitors.name: Amazon
competitors.headline: White Friday runs 12 days, with Prime at Dhs16 a month
body: Amazon UAE's White Friday runs 19–30 November, with up to 60% off Amazon devices and up to 50% off home appliances. A Bazaar code gives up to 25% off orders of seven or more units.
Prime costs Dhs16 a month or Dhs140 a year, and fast delivery is part of the offer.
competitors.soWhat: Amazon keeps its own parcels in-house. Our share of this peak comes from sellers and brands not on Amazon's own network.

competitors.name: noon
competitors.headline: Yellow Friday pushes 15-minute delivery on noon Minutes
body: noon's Yellow Friday runs 19–30 November with up to 90% off and up to 80% off on noon Minutes. noon says delivery can take as little as 15 minutes.
Tabby and Tamara offer six months at 0% interest during the sale.
competitors.soWhat: Quick commerce sets customer expectations. Our same-day and next-day offers need clear cut-off times this week.

competitors.name: Aramex (baseline)
competitors.headline: Q3 net profit Dh48m on record Dh1.98bn revenue
body: Still our latest figures: Q3 net profit rose to Dh48 million from Dh5.2 million, and revenue rose 24% to a record Dh1.98 billion. Freight forwarding led growth; gross margin was 21% against 23.2%.
competitors.soWhat: With Dubai air export rates up 83%, forwarding margin depends on how fast we pass buy-rate rises through.

opportunities.title: Oman–UAE road as a product
opportunities.text: Duqm, Sohar and the Green Corridors now carry Gulf and Saudi-bound cargo. Package a priced, scheduled Oman–UAE–Saudi road service.

opportunities.title: Dubai outbound air yield
opportunities.text: Dubai–Europe and Dubai–US rates are up over 80%. Spot quotes can carry the market rate.

opportunities.title: Peak-week sellers off Amazon
opportunities.text: Brands and marketplace sellers outside Amazon's own network need extra capacity to 30 November.

opportunities.title: December returns
opportunities.text: Two 12-day sales mean a returns wave in early December. Offer a returns pick-up bundle now.

opportunities.title: Europe belly space returns
opportunities.text: Lufthansa group flights restart on 25 November. Lock in allocations early before others do.

watchouts.title: No cargo transits for three days
watchouts.text: No cargo ships above 1,000 dwt crossed Hormuz on 19–21 November. Sea-dependent customers will need more road and air.

watchouts.title: Attacks spreading to Bahrain
watchouts.text: Iranian aerial attacks on Bahrain add risk to northern Gulf road and air routes.

watchouts.title: Saudi air volumes falling
watchouts.text: Air cargo into Saudi Arabia is down 33% against early October. Check Saudi air forecasts and commitments.

watchouts.title: Peak-week service failures
watchouts.text: Sales volumes plus 15-minute delivery promises raise the risk of missed SLAs and complaints.

watchouts.title: Rates may soften in December
watchouts.text: Returning European belly space could pull Dubai–Europe rates down. Avoid buying long fixed capacity at today's peak.

moves.title: Daily Dubai outbound air rate card
moves.text: Reprice Dubai–Europe and Dubai–US spot air daily while rates sit over 80% above last year.

moves.title: Launch an Oman–UAE–Saudi road offer
moves.text: Price a scheduled road service via Sohar or Duqm into the UAE and on to Saudi Arabia, and send it to Gulf sea-exposed accounts.

moves.title: Book Lufthansa group allocations
moves.text: Talk to Lufthansa Cargo before 25 November about Dubai–Frankfurt belly space for December.

moves.title: Peak-week capacity for non-Amazon sellers
moves.text: Call top e-commerce sellers today with extra pick-up slots and clear cut-off times to 30 November.

moves.title: Returns bundle for early December
moves.text: Prepare a returns pick-up and processing rate for sellers ahead of the post-sale wave.

moves.title: Review Saudi air commitments
moves.text: With Saudi air weight down 33%, check minimum-volume deals and shift spare demand to road.

note: Read from today's news. Check against our own numbers before acting.
